findings.summary: The global and commerce surfaces remain light when the user requests a dark colour scheme.
findings.evidence: The prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshot remains white, the computed body surface is rgb(255, 254, 251), and the CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme, light-dark(), or color-scheme support.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and map surface, text, border, image treatment, and browser chrome tokens through prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Cookie consent obscures the primary content on every first visit, consuming almost the entire mobile viewport.
findings.evidence: Initial desktop, listing, product, and 360x800 screenshots show the consent panel covering the main content. On mobile only the header and consent text/actions are visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-blocking consent surface for optional cookies, retain equally prominent accept/reject actions, and keep the core page readable before a choice.

findings.summary: The consent modal is an ad-hoc div with role=dialog rather than the platform dialog primitive.
findings.evidence: DOM probes across global and UK pages found a visible DIV role=dialog with no aria-modal and no native dialog element.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog for a truly modal consent decision, with showModal(), platform focus containment, Escape handling where policy permits, and an explicit accessible name.

findings.summary: Page and route changes do not use View Transitions, so template changes are abrupt.
findings.evidence: CSS probes on the homepage, article, listing, and product found no view-transition rules or names.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document View Transitions for global story navigation and scoped same-document transitions for commerce state changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: The listing exposes tooltip overlays but does not use CSS anchor positioning or fallback positions.
findings.evidence: The listing accessibility probe found multiple role=tooltip elements while CSS inspection found no anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Anchor tooltips and transient menus to their trigger with CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks, retaining the current robust fallback for unsupported browsers.

findings.summary: Several interactive targets are smaller than the recommended touch target size.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed target-size on the global homepage. DOM probes found a 32x28 menu-adjacent button and many 40x40 commerce controls, below a 44x44 target.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase hit areas to at least 44x44 CSS pixels or provide sufficient spacing, without shrinking the visible icon.

findings.summary: Accessible names and list semantics are inconsistent on representative pages.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found visible-label/accessibility-name mismatches on both global and product pages and two malformed list structures on the homepage; the global probe also identified an unnamed visible button.
findings.suggestedFix: Make accessible names begin with or match visible labels, give every icon button an explicit name, and ensure list containers have only li/script/template direct children.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is slow on both the global homepage and product detail template.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP at 7.0s on the homepage and 6.2s on the product page. A separate desktop trace measured 1.47s and 2.84s respectively, showing the mobile/throttled path is the risk.
findings.suggestedFix: Identify each mobile LCP element, preload only the winning candidate, set fetchpriority=high where appropriate, remove discovery delays, and defer non-critical media and consent code.

findings.summary: The commerce product template has a highly fragmented critical resource graph.
findings.evidence: The product HAR recorded 246 requests, including 134 scripts and 57 stylesheets, with 1.86MB transferred. Many parser-inserted, VeryHigh-priority stylesheets appear in the critical path; mobile LCP was 6.2s.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate and route-scope critical CSS, reduce parser-blocking stylesheet fan-out, defer non-critical feature fragments, and prioritize only resources needed for the product hero and purchase controls.

findings.summary: The product template ships substantial unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 337KiB unused JavaScript and 135KiB unused CSS on the product page; individual bundles were 72% to 99% unused in the measured load.
findings.suggestedFix: Split reviews, recommendations, account, experimentation, and lower-funnel features by interaction/visibility, and eliminate duplicate or template-wide CSS from the initial product route.

findings.summary: The product page logs an uncaught experiment-store initialization error.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured console.error: “[expt-store] exptSDK.init did not return a client” from zip-store-DdpxZMer.js.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle a missing experiment client as an expected fallback state, avoid logging it as an error, and add a regression test for blocked or unavailable experiment services.

findings.summary: Many product images omit intrinsic width and height attributes.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 15 of 26 product-page images without width/height attributes, including the primary product gallery images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width and height for each image variant (or a stable aspect-ratio wrapper) so layout reservation is explicit before image metadata arrives.

findings.summary: Large first-party scripts have missing or broken source maps.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported six source-map failures, including ratings/reviews and shopping-cart agent bundles.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish matching source maps for production bundles or remove broken sourceMappingURL references while retaining maps in the error-monitoring pipeline.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced security and privacy policies are absent, and one consent cookie is not Secure.
findings.evidence: Headers include strong CSP, HSTS, and frame-ancestors, but omit X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy. The cookies primitive found OptanonConsent set without Secure.
findings.suggestedFix: Add nosniff, a deliberate Referrer-Policy and restrictive Permissions-Policy; mark OptanonConsent Secure; retain the existing CSP/HSTS/frame-ancestors protections.

findings.summary: The app-like commerce experience is neither installable nor equipped with an offline fallback.
findings.evidence: Homepage, listing, and product probes found no web app manifest and no controlling service worker. The commerce journey depends on networked fragments.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a manifest and a narrowly scoped service worker that serves an honest offline shell, preserves recently viewed product information where appropriate, and gives retry guidance for network-only actions.

findings.summary: The global editorial homepage relies heavily on legacy image formats and eagerly starts some below-fold media.
findings.evidence: The images primitive classified 39 of 40 images as JPG/PNG/GIF, found seven below-fold images without lazy loading and six oversized images. Lighthouse measured a 2.51MiB page load.
findings.suggestedFix: Negotiate AVIF/WebP sources, lazy-load non-LCP editorial media, right-size responsive candidates, and avoid starting below-fold videos until near the viewport or user intent.

findings.summary: Editorial articles lack article-specific structured data and identify themselves as generic websites in Open Graph.
findings.evidence: The ASPUDDEN article has useful title, description, canonical and Open Graph image, but no JSON-LD and og:type is website rather than article.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit schema.org Article JSON-LD matching the visible headline, description, image, dates and publisher, and use og:type=article with accurate article metadata.
